data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a gross strengthening of $5.582 million in prior year claims reserves. This adverse development is primarily attributed to natural catastrophe events and large losses, specifically the impact of 2017 catastrophe events (Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, Maria, and Mexican earthquakes) on the 2016 year of account, as well as US weather-related events including flood and hail losses and Hurricane Matthew from 2016.
raw_causal_phrases: deterioration of $5,582,000 in claims reserves established at the prior year

The 2016 year of account has a forecast loss in the range of 10% to 20% on stamp capacity at the 24 month stage. This forecast result reflects the impact of the catastrophe events of 2017 together with an increase in US weather related events in 2016, mostly in respect of flood and hail losses.

The 2016 account has been heavily impacted by the 2017 third quarter catastrophe losses, notably hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria that hit the Caribbean and the US. Two Mexican earthquakes in September resulted in further losses.

In addition the 2016 calendar year loss experience was higher than expected for the first twelve months with a number of large and catastrophe losses including Hurricane Matthew and a number of flood and hail losses.
